# Employee National Insurance, in plain English

Figures: 2026-27. The rules this text is printed from are proved equal to the model's own definitions for every input and every parameter set (`class1Weekly_eval`, `class1For_eval`); see [README.md](README.md) for what that does and does not cover.

## Employee National Insurance, Class 1 (SSCBA 1992 s8)

Employee National Insurance on your pay for the week is charged in bands. Each rate applies only to the part of your pay for the week that falls in its band:

| Part of your pay for the week | Rate |
| --- | --- |
| The first £242 | 0% (no contribution) |
| Over £242, up to £967 | 8% (main primary percentage) |
| Over £967 | 2% (additional primary percentage) |

**Earnings** means what your employer pays you from the job for the week, before income tax and before any pension contributions taken from your pay. Pensions, savings interest and dividends are not earnings and carry no National Insurance. This is for an employee aged 16 to State Pension age on category letter A.

These are the weekly figures. If you are paid monthly, or once a year (as some company directors are), the same bands apply with these figures instead:

| Paid | Primary threshold | Upper earnings limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Weekly | £242 | £967 |
| Monthly | £1,048 | £4,189 |
| Yearly | £12,570 | £50,270 |

National Insurance is worked out for each pay period separately, so with uneven pay the year's total depends on how the pay is spread.

For example:

| Earnings | Employee National Insurance |
| --- | --- |
| £200 | £0 |
| £242 | £0 |
| £500 | £20.64 |
| £967 | £58 |
| £1,500 | £68.66 |
